documents.body:
Annual exam.

Interval: no illnesses this year. One cold in January, rode it out, didn't need albuterol more than usual. Inhaler use ~2x/wk. No exacerbations since joining. Still smoking about a pack a day; 1 ppd since 25.

Meds: tiotropium 18 mcg daily, albuterol prn, amlodipine 5 mg daily. NKDA.

ROS: negative except chronic exertional dyspnea, unchanged.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. NAD. HEENT clear, no adenopathy. Heart regular, no murmurs. Lungs: diminished breath sounds at bases, prolonged expiration, no wheeze. Abd benign. Ext: no edema. Skin: no lesions of concern.

Screens: PHQ-2 1 (a little stressed at work), AUDIT-C 2.

A/P
- COPD GOLD 2: stable. Same regimen.
- HTN: controlled.
- Tobacco: still precontemplative. Discussed again; door open.
- HM: colonoscopy 2028. Cervical co-test due 2024 - will do next year. Mammo and LDCT in Nov, both negative last year. Flu and COVID in the fall.
- Labs today: CMP, CBC, lipids.

RTC fall.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: vulvar itching, spotting.

HPI: 55F, booked as a flu shot visit, then told the MA she wanted to ask about something. About 5 months of itching "down there" that has slowly gotten worse, on the right side. Over the last couple of months some spotting of blood on her underwear on and off, and a discharge with a bad odor. Hoped it would settle on its own; embarrassed, kept putting it off. Postmenopausal. No fever, no urinary symptoms, no groin swelling she has noticed. Hx genital warts treated in the 90s/2000s; mother had cervical cancer, sister CIN II.

Exam (chaperoned by MA): right labia majora with an ulcerated, friable lesion, roughly 3 cm, bleeds lightly with contact. Left side and perineum without visible lesion on external inspection. No palpable inguinal nodes on either side. Speculum exam not done today.

A/P
1. Ulcerated right vulvar lesion - needs tissue diagnosis. Concerning for neoplasia given appearance, HPV history and smoking. Urgent gynecology referral placed and I called their office; they will see her within a few weeks. Explained to her honestly that it has to be biopsied and that the biopsy will tell us what it is. She is worried but okay with the plan.
2. Flu vaccine given.
3. COPD/HTN: no changes today.

Will call her when the gyn note comes in.

reports.conclusion: BI-RADS 1. Negative. Next screening in 12 months.

documents.title: Gynecology Consultation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GYNECOLOGY - CONSULTATION LETTER
Date of service: 11/20/2023
Re: Evelyn Murphy, DOB 11/28/1967

Thank you for referring Ms. Murphy, a 55-year-old woman, for a vulvar lesion.

She describes six months of vulvar itching that has steadily worsened, with intermittent bleeding and a malodorous vaginal discharge.

History: COPD, hypertension, tobacco dependence. Remote treatment of condylomata with excision and cryotherapy over the 1990s-2000s; laparoscopic cholecystectomy 2010.
Medications: albuterol HFA as needed, tiotropium 18 mcg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: mother with cervical cancer at 42; father with lung cancer at 58; sister with CIN II.
Social: smokes, about 30 pack-years.

Examination: On the right labium majus there is a 3 cm ulcerated mass that is friable on contact. Inguinal lymph nodes are not palpable bilaterally. Remainder of the external genitalia without other gross lesion; vagina and cervix appear normal; bimanual exam unremarkable.

Procedure: After local anesthesia, punch biopsy of the lesion was obtained and sent to pathology. Hemostasis with silver nitrate. Tolerated well.

Impression: Ulcerated right vulvar mass, suspicious for malignancy. Pathology pending; I will contact her and you with the result. If malignant she will be referred to gynecologic oncology.

Gynecology

conditions.label: Malignant neoplasm of labium majus
conditions.note: right labia majora, biopsy-proven squamous cell carcinoma

reports.text:
SPECIMEN: Vulva, right labium majus, punch biopsy.
GROSS: Received in formalin, a tan-pink punch of skin, 0.4 cm in diameter, entirely submitted.
MICROSCOPIC: Sections show squamous mucosa with invasive nests of atypical squamous cells infiltrating the underlying stroma, with surface ulceration. The base of the biopsy is involved.
reports.conclusion: Vulva, right, punch biopsy: INVASIVE SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA.

documents.body: Called pt re: vulvar biopsy (SCC). She heard from gyn Friday. Understandably shaken; has told her sister. Gyn onc consult is set for next Tuesday. She wanted to know if smoking matters for healing - yes, and any cut-down helps. She'll think about it.

documents.title: Gynecologic Oncology Consultation
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
GYNECOLOGIC ONCOLOGY NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Visit date: 12/05/2023
Patient: Evelyn Murphy (DOB 11/28/1967)
Referring: outside gynecology; PCP copied

Diagnosis: Invasive squamous cell carcinoma of the right vulva, on biopsy 11/20/2023.

HPI: 56-year-old with roughly six months of right vulvar pruritus, intermittent bleeding and malodorous discharge. Biopsy at gynecology showed invasive SCC.

PMH: COPD on tiotropium and albuterol; hypertension on amlodipine. Prior condyloma treatment. Lap chole 2010.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Social: current smoker, 1 ppd.
Family: mother cervical cancer; father lung cancer; sister CIN II.

Exam: Well appearing. Groins: no palpable inguinal or femoral adenopathy bilaterally. Vulva: 3 cm ulcerated lesion of the right labium majus, well lateral to the midline, not involving the clitoris, urethra or anus. Healing biopsy site. Vagina and cervix normal on speculum. Rectovaginal exam without nodularity.

Assessment: Clinically early-stage right lateral vulvar SCC, unifocal, under 4 cm, groins clinically negative.

Plan:
1. CT chest, abdomen and pelvis with contrast for staging.
2. If no nodal or distant disease, right radical local excision (radical partial vulvectomy) with right inguinal sentinel lymph node biopsy. Risks reviewed including wound separation, infection, lymphedema, and change in sensation; she wishes to proceed.
3. Pre-operative evaluation with her PCP given COPD.
4. Strongly encouraged smoking cessation before surgery.

Gynecologic Oncology

documents.title: Pre-operative Evaluation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PRE-OP EVALUATION
Procedure: right radical local excision of vulva with right inguinal sentinel lymph node biopsy, gynecologic oncology, planned 01/09/2024, general anesthesia.

Reviewed gyn onc consult and staging CT (no nodes, no distant disease, no lung nodule).

Cardiopulmonary: walks a few blocks and climbs 2 flights with some breathlessness, stops to rest at the top, no chest pain, no syncope. >4 METs. No exacerbation in the past year, no steroids. Albuterol ~2x/week. Tiotropium daily.
Smoking: down to about 3/4 ppd this month, she says. Encouraged to stop entirely at least the week before and after surgery.
No personal or family hx of anesthesia problems. No bleeding history. No anticoagulants or supplements.

Meds: tiotropium 18 mcg daily, albuterol prn, amlodipine 5 mg daily. NKDA.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Airway: Mallampati II, normal neck mobility, own teeth. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs with prolonged expiration, clear, no wheeze. No edema.

ECG: NSR 74, normal.
CBC, BMP today.

Assessment: 56F with stable moderate COPD (GOLD 2) and controlled HTN for low-to-intermediate risk surgery. No active cardiac conditions. Acceptable risk to proceed.
Recommendations:
- Take tiotropium and amlodipine the morning of surgery. Bring albuterol.
- Incentive spirometry and early ambulation post-op.
- Smoking abstinence around surgery as above.

Copy to gynecologic oncology.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Gynecologic Oncology
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 01/09/2024  Discharged: 01/10/2024
Service: Gynecologic Oncology

Diagnosis: Squamous cell carcinoma of the right vulva.
Procedure 01/09/2024: Right radical local excision of the vulva (radical partial vulvectomy) with right inguinal sentinel lymph node biopsy after technetium and blue dye injection. Two right inguinal sentinel nodes identified and removed. Primary closure of the vulvar defect. EBL 50 mL. No complications.

Hospital course: Uneventful overnight stay. Pain controlled on oral medication. Voiding spontaneously after catheter removal on POD 1. Ambulating. Used her own inhalers; no respiratory issues. Tolerating diet.

Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge medications: oxycodone-acetaminophen 5/325 mg, 1 tab q6h prn pain (#20). Continue home tiotropium, albuterol prn, amlodipine 5 mg.
Instructions: Sitz baths twice daily and after bowel movements, keep incisions clean and dry, no intercourse or tampons until cleared, no heavy lifting for 2 weeks. Call for fever, spreading redness, wound drainage, or groin swelling.
Follow-up: Gynecologic oncology in 3 weeks; final pathology to be reviewed then.

Gynecologic Oncology

documents.title: Post-discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Post-discharge call. Home since yesterday. Pain is manageable, took 2 of the oxycodone pills yesterday and 1 overnight, none yet today. Doing sitz baths. No fever. Incision without drainage per pt. Breathing at baseline. Bowels not yet moved - advised fluids, walking. She has not smoked since Monday and wants to try to keep it that way; encouraged. Knows to call gyn onc for wound concerns. Post-op visit 1/30.

reports.text:
SPECIMENS:
A. Vulva, right, radical local excision (stitch marks anterior margin).
B. Right inguinal sentinel lymph node #1.
C. Right inguinal sentinel lymph node #2.

DIAGNOSIS:
A. Invasive squamous cell carcinoma, HPV-associated (p16 block-positive).
   Tumor size: 3.0 cm in greatest dimension.
   Depth of invasion: 4 mm.
   Lymphovascular invasion: not identified.
   Margins: negative for invasive carcinoma; closest margin (deep) 10 mm.
B. One lymph node, negative for carcinoma (0/1), including on cytokeratin immunostain.
C. One lymph node, negative for carcinoma (0/1), including on cytokeratin immunostain.

SYNOPTIC: pT1b pN0 (sn). FIGO (2021) stage IB.
reports.conclusion: Right vulvar invasive squamous cell carcinoma, HPV-associated, 3.0 cm, 4 mm depth of invasion, margins negative, sentinel lymph nodes 0/2. FIGO stage IB.

documents.title: Gynecologic Oncology Post-op Visit
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
GYNECOLOGIC ONCOLOGY - POST-OPERATIVE VISIT
Date: 01/30/2024

Ms. Murphy is three weeks out from right radical local excision of the vulva and right inguinal sentinel lymph node biopsy. She is doing well; off narcotics since the first week. Mild tenderness at the groin incision, resolving. No fever, drainage or leg swelling. She reports she has not smoked since surgery.

Exam: Vulvar incision well healed, no separation or erythema. Right groin incision clean, no seroma. No lower extremity edema.

Pathology reviewed with her: invasive SCC, HPV-associated, 3.0 cm, DOI 4 mm, no LVSI, margins negative (closest 10 mm), sentinel nodes 0/2. FIGO 2021 stage IB.

Plan: No adjuvant therapy indicated. Surveillance with history and exam every 3 months for 2 years, then every 6 months, alternating between our office and her gynecologist. Imaging only for symptoms. Advised to report any new vulvar itching, lump, bleeding or groin swelling between visits. Continued smoking abstinence strongly encouraged. Cleared for normal activity.

Gynecologic Oncology

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical.

Interval history: right vulvar SCC dx 11/2023, s/p right radical local excision + R inguinal SLN 1/9/24 - stage IB, margins neg, nodes 0/2, no adjuvant tx. Gyn onc surveillance q3mo, first in April. Recovered well.

Tobacco: stayed off cigarettes about 5 weeks after surgery, restarted in February when work got busy. Now ~1 ppd again. Disappointed in herself. We talked about it without lecturing - she knows. Not ready to try medication. Will revisit.

COPD: no exacerbations. Albuterol 1-3x/week. Tiotropium daily.
HTN: amlodipine 5, no side effects.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. NAD. No cervical/supraclavicular nodes. Heart regular. Lungs prolonged expiration, clear. Abd soft. Groins without palpable nodes, healed R groin incision. Ext no edema.

PHQ-2 1. AUDIT-C 1.

A/P
1. Vulvar SCC stage IB, s/p excision - surveillance per gyn onc; cervical screening will be handled at her gyn visits.
2. COPD GOLD 2 - stable.
3. HTN - controlled.
4. Tobacco - relapsed after brief quit. Encouraged; will keep offering.
5. HM: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c. Mammo 11/2023 neg. LDCT: staging CT 12/2023 showed no nodules; next LDCT December. Colonoscopy 2028.

RTC fall.
